definitions.explanation: Fruit whose moisture has been removed through sun-drying, hot-air drying, or freeze-drying. The formal, written-Japanese equivalent of the more common everyday term ドライフルーツ.

examples.japanese: {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{様々|さまざま}→様々：01559_samazama⟧な{乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{扱|あつか}っている→扱う：01862_atsukau⟧。
examples.english: This shop carries various kinds of dried fruit.

examples.japanese: {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{栄養|えいよう}→栄養：01882_eiyou⟧{価|か}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}く→高い：00500_takai⟧、⟦{保存|ほぞん}→保存：03626_hozon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{向|む}いている→向く：02304_muku⟧。
examples.english: Dried fruit is high in nutritional value and keeps well.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧ ('drying; dehydration') and ⟦{果実|かじつ}→果実：00146_kajitsu⟧ ('fruit'). A formal term for dried fruit, appearing mainly in labeling, ingredient lists, nutritional writing, and food-industry texts.

USAGE:
- In everyday conversation, Japanese speakers overwhelmingly prefer the loanword ⟦ドライフルーツ→ドライフルーツ：20795_doraifuruutsu⟧.
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ} appears on packaging ingredient lists, customs documents, food-safety regulations, and nutritional articles.
- Common examples of dried fruit: ⟦レーズン→レーズン：12843_reezun⟧ (raisins), プルーン (prunes), ⟦ドライ→ドライ：11147_dorai⟧マンゴー (dried mango), ⟦{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}→干し柿：28314_hoshigaki⟧ (dried persimmon), ⟦{干|ほ}し→干す：00115_hosu⟧ブドウ (dried grapes/raisins).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧: to eat dried fruit
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{加|くわ}える→加える：01941_kuwaeru⟧: to add dried fruit (to a recipe)
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}{入|い}り: containing dried fruit
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}ミックス: dried fruit mix

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ドライフルーツ→ドライフルーツ：20795_doraifuruutsu⟧: dried fruit — everyday, casual loanword; the default term in speech and most food packaging.
- ⟦{干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}→干し果物：26765_hoshikudamono⟧: dried fruit — native Japanese expression using the verb ⟦{干|ほ}す→干す：00115_hosu⟧ ('to dry in the sun'); somewhat old-fashioned.
- ⟦{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}→干し柿：28314_hoshigaki⟧: dried persimmon — a specific traditional Japanese example.
- ⟦{果実|かじつ}→果実：00146_kajitsu⟧: fruit — the formal counterpart of ⟦{果物|くだもの}→果物：00509_kudamono⟧.
